RESEARCH EXPERIENCE

PhD Student in Neuroscience
August 2020 - Present
Location: University of Texas at Austin
Advisor: Dr. Thibaud Taillefumier
Projects: I develop an analytical framework using a conductance- based model to understand how input synchrony, synaptic strength, and network structure shape neural variability. By linking subthreshold and spiking variability to input correlations and intrinsic neuronal properties, the work reveals how cellular and network mechanisms jointly regulate the statistical structure of cortical activity.
Technical Associate
January 2019 - June 2020
Location: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
Advisor: Dr. Carmen Varela
Projects: I studied the effects of eszopiclone and zolpidem, two sleep medications, where we find opposing effects on hippocampal ripple activity and neuronal firing in rats, which may explain their differing impacts on memory in humans. While zolpidem enhances ripple density and preserves spiking, eszopiclone suppresses both, suggesting that sleep medications can differentially regulate neural dynamics critical for memory consolidation.
Master's Student in Neuroscience
July 2017 - December 2019
Location: SUNY Stony Brook University
Advisor: Dr. Il Memming Park
Projects: I developed and analyzed biophysically inspired integrate-and-fire neuron models to capture a diverse range of spiking dynamics, including intermittent firing and bursting behavior. This work contributed to understanding how intrinsic neuronal properties shape complex firing patterns observed in the brain.
Undergraduate Student in Physics
August 2016 - May 2017
Location: SUNY Stony Brook University
Advisor: Dr. Il Memming Park
Projects: I used Fourier analysis to investigate detection methods for identifying phase-amplitude coupling (PAC) between oscillating signals in neural systems. This work aimed to improve our understanding of how different brain rhythms interact and how such coupling may play a role in neural communication and information processing.

FELLOWSHIPS

Chateaubriand Fellow
November 2024 - April 2025
Award: $6500
Advisor: Dr. David Hansel
Description: Prestigious fellowship awarded by the French Foreign Affairs Ministry, fully funding a 6-month independent research project at Université de Paris, France. The project, titled “Emergence and Self-Consistency of Spike Correlations in Recurrent Neural Networks,” involved close collaboration with leading computational neuroscience researchers at the host institution. This immersive experience not only deepened my expertise in neural network dynamics but also significantly contributed original findings and theoretical advancements that were integrated into my doctoral dissertation, strengthening its overall impact and scope.
